items.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013
items.q: I wrote an entire tune based off of that beat, and I called it “Soulful Brother Gillespie.”

ctx.x: But I wrote an entire tune based off of that beat, and I called it “Soulful Brother Gillespie.” And I even expanded it into a big band arrangement. So that’s to say I’ve composed off of many influences, from something like that or I might hear the melody first. I wrote a tune on my first CD the title track is called “Slim Goody.” And I heard that melody while I was on the subway when I was living in New York, I was traveling on the subway to visit my girlfriend at the time. And it was before cell phones. And so I…

strange on the subway. So when I got to my subway stop I went to a pay phone and called my answer machine and sang it into the answer machine so I wouldn’t forget it. Because you know you’ll think of something like at night when you go to sleep and your mind is open. And — man I really like that melody, okay, when I get up tomorrow I’m going to write it down. And you get up the next morning and say what was that thing I thought about last night, and it’s gone. You can’t even think about it.
